9b6180ff-532c-4ca8-8565-62328eb30f79.headline: Big objectives. Broken base.
9b6180ff-532c-4ca8-8565-62328eb30f79.team: We secured major buffs and produced a dominant fight, but the late objective sequence ended with heavy deaths before the base losses piled up. Winning a neutral does not make the whole exchange good; that buff was no condom for the base.

focus.title: Call the exit before the take
focus.action: Before the next major objective, agree where the team retreats and who handles the base defense.

perPlayer.9ec9a569-ce18-4a46-8f58-98d28b3b75d1: Crunch kept the farm moving, then spent too much time dead to make that gold useful. Keep the income; review the late death for an earlier exit and take that correction into the next game. A full wallet does fuck-all from the death screen.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Narbash delivered the healing, but the repeated deaths need scrutiny, not a support excuse. Keep that output. Review which deaths actually protected teammates and which could have been avoided, then fix the avoidable ones. Being the healer is not a license to donate his ass.
perPlayer.4adab30d-c60a-4995-a659-c46fe0768ed2: Serath supplied the damage and objective pressure this team needed. Keep it, but fix the thin ward placement: put vision on a safe approach before the next neutral setup. Strong damage does not make information optional.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Howitzer contributed damage and still finished with the team's worst death count. Keep the damage; review those deaths for a recurring decision and change it if one emerges. This is the priority before another build tweak. A fashionable build is not a fucking respawn discount.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Eden's farm and survival both fell short. Make reliable income the recovery priority: prioritize reachable waves between fights and review the midgame death for a safer route. Recovery needs income that does not come with another death attached.

90a87d12-ad66-4c03-8137-3999c53e0999.headline: Too little return from the fights.
90a87d12-ad66-4c03-8137-3999c53e0999.team: The enemy won most recorded fight sequences and took towers while we took none. The deaths before Fangtooth and the later tower loss deserve more attention than chasing a different shopping list.

focus.title: Set the contest condition
focus.action: Before the next Fangtooth setup, agree what must be ready to contest and what makes the team back off.

perPlayer.9681844e-07b6-4b92-8247-00a5a393b35a: Gadget led the team's damage and kept farming near the usual baseline. Keep that foundation, but do not wave away the death before Fangtooth because the damage total looks good. Review whether a safer position or earlier retreat was available and take the answer into the next setup.
perPlayer.8cc8b136-b5f5-4d0b-be88-2a425b3927e3: Aurora's economy never got going, and no completed item is a serious problem. Find where the income stopped, including farm access and downtime, before arguing about the build. Fix the income bottleneck first; a different shopping list cannot spend gold that never arrived.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock led ward placement, but farm and survival were rough. Keep the warding and prioritize reachable waves between fights. Review the death around the tower loss for a concrete correction. The gun needs gold, not a fucking sympathy card.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Yin delivered the team's strongest kill and objective output. Keep that pressure. Review whether a safer approach was available before Fangtooth, then carry any clear correction into the next setup.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel supplied the mitigation, but vision placement was sparse. Keep the frontline contribution and put wards on safe objective approaches before the next setup. Judge the coverage, not just the count. Dying to place a cosmetic ward is not an improvement.

16.call: The 0-3 sequence ended as an Outer Tower fell; enemy Mini Prime followed.

05ad9a23-e6d6-42ec-893d-726fdb33a84c.headline: A proper win: the squad broke the base and finished the job.
05ad9a23-e6d6-42ec-893d-726fdb33a84c.team: Major objectives stayed with the squad, and the closing fights produced a demolished enemy base. The late outer-tower loss barely interrupted the finish; this was control with an ending, not endless foreplay around the river.

focus.title: Call the finish before the chase
focus.action: After the next won fight, the shot-caller should name the safest reachable structure and check the wave and team health; if the push is unsafe, call the reset immediately.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Wukong did excellent objective work and useful ward clearing. Keep both. Ward placement was poor, so put a ward on a safe approach before the next commitment. The jungle cannot keep running on good intentions and a flimsy condom of vision.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock delivered strong carry damage. Keep that output, but review the late death instead of letting the win bury it. Before advancing into enemy jungle next game, confirm nearby peel and a route back. More damage is useless once the carry is dead.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Scarlett supplied defense and strong warding, but no objective damage. Keep the defensive contribution and warding; make the next post-fight assignment explicit: guard the approach or hit the objective. Call the job and do it so the team knows what is covered.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel contributed to takedowns without dying. Keep that shit. The next improvement is vision denial: check contested approaches with a teammate and clear reachable enemy wards before the objective setup. A clean combat game should come with a cleaner approach to the next fight.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Belica delivered strong damage, few deaths and objective contribution. Keep that shit. After the next safe fight win, keep adding damage to the objective once the approach is covered. This is a performance to repeat, not a reason to start tinkering with everything.

20.4.call: A 3-1 kill cluster ended at 20:55; an enemy outer tower fell eleven seconds later. The follow-through mattered.

24.7.call: Five enemy deaths, no allied deaths in this cluster. Two inner towers and two inhibitors fell from 25:07 through 25:46. That was the decisive damage to the base.

27.8.call: Four enemy deaths without an allied death in the closing cluster. The Core fell at 28:33. Finish secured.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Wukong recorded strong objective damage while equipped with Manta Scythe, Infernum, The Perforator and Painweaver. No comparison here isolates their value, and the missing-magic-resist flag alone does not establish a build mistake.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Imperator match the recorded comparison core. Nothing in the death event establishes that a different item would have prevented it.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Mistmeadow Buckler, Terminus and Tainted Bastion differ from the comparison core. The mitigation total supports a defensive contribution, but cannot isolate item value or prove the build caused zero objective damage.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Caustica and Noxia were equipped. The performance supports keeping this as a useful baseline, not declaring the combination optimal or attributing the win to Caustica.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Fire Blossom, Xenia, Dynamo and Prophecy accompanied a deathless support game. That result does not isolate their individual value or prove the comparison core worse.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: This review does not model Steel's Eternal contribution; no claim about its effectiveness follows from these totals.

33247683-e032-4d42-aa29-19fa4f201ce1.headline: Good win. The early duo deaths still need cleaning up.
33247683-e032-4d42-aa29-19fa4f201ce1.team: The squad took structures without losing any and secured Mini Prime despite conceding Fangtooth. The duo recovery mattered, but a win does not spray enough deodorant over the early deaths to make them disappear.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Wukong delivered objective pressure without dying. Keep that standard, but fix the thin ward placement. Put a safe approach ward down before starting the next objective. Good pressure needs information; the win does not make that job optional.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock supplied useful kills after Mini Prime, but repeated early deaths made this a mixed game. Keep the productive pressure and review those opening deaths for one concrete adjustment. Fix that before changing items. Winning does not turn a rough opening into good play.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Greystone brought warding, objective damage and survival. That is useful work. Keep the warding; next game, place vision on safe approaches and help finish the take once the route is covered. Repeat the contribution instead of chasing a prettier scoreline.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Belica led hero damage without dying, but recorded no objective damage. Keep the combat standard and look for a safe objective hit after the next won fight. The damage needs somewhere useful to go once enemy heroes stop volunteering.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Riktor had a rough opening and cleared no wards. Make vision denial a concrete job next game: check the objective approach with a teammate and clear reachable wards before committing. The win is not a reason to leave that part of the support job unfinished.

12.9.call: Mini Prime fell before Murdock killed Phase and Zinx; an outer tower followed the kills. Kill credit does not establish who else was present.

15.3.call: This kill cluster went 1-2. No timestamped positions establish who could join, so the feed cannot justify the old claim that teammates were pinned elsewhere or the fight was a local 5v5.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Manta Scythe and Infernum were equipped. No winning-core comparison exists for Wukong; the missing-magic-resist flag does not establish a costly mistake.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Lightning Hawk and Vanquisher match the first two items in the comparison core. Purchase times are estimates, so the report cannot claim an early Vanquisher spike.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Overlord was equipped when the short match ended. Missing later comparison items is not a demonstrated mistake; no observed purchase timing establishes what could have been completed.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Combustion and Wraith Leggings were equipped. Estimated item timings cannot prove the build landed exactly on curve, and this match does not isolate a benefit from replacing either item.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Dynamo and Xenia match two comparison-core items. The inventory alone does not explain the early deaths.

focus.title: Make the objective call before committing
focus.action: Before contesting the next major objective, the shot-caller should confirm who can actually join and call either the contest or a specific cross-map trade.

7f2d94e6-5d00-4927-9818-ee86d6f6349f.headline: Dominant win. The carry delivered; vision still needs work.
7f2d94e6-5d00-4927-9818-ee86d6f6349f.team: Murdock supplied the main damage while Wukong drove objective output and the squad took both recorded Fangtooths. The fighting and objective results earned the win, but the support vision contribution still needs to catch up; smashing faces is only part of the job.

focus.title: Give the objective setup a vision job
focus.action: Before the next major objective, the shot-caller should assign one teammate to clear the approach and another to cover them before the team starts it.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Wukong delivered kills and team-leading objective damage without dying. Keep the pressure and survival. Ward placement was thin, so add a safe ward on the exit route before the next commitment. Plan the way out as deliberately as the way in.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock carried the damage and kept deaths low. Keep that standard. In the next fight, hit the nearest safe target and leave enough room to respond when the enemy turns. Do not turn a strong carry game into a highlight hunt.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Scarlett contributed warding but no objective damage. Keep the vision and make the next post-fight job explicit: protect the approach or hit the objective. Tell the team which job is covered and follow through. Useful work should have a clear purpose.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Belica's early death to Bayle is the decision to review. Work out what made it possible and choose one concrete adjustment for the next match. Do that before touching the build. The shopping list is not a substitute for fixing a bad sequence.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel contributed to takedowns and led mitigation, but ward placement was sparse. Keep the fighting contribution and place available wards on safe objective approaches before the next setup. Check coverage with the team. Landing the engage does not tick every box on the support job.
